content.text:
**Finding submitted: deviation (high severity, T4C).**

**What the document does:**
- **§14.2.2 "At-Will Termination by PB"** — PB's only convenience right, but double-gated: unavailable until SFJ has paid/incurred **$60 million** of Development Costs, and it closes on receipt of the first Regulatory Approval. Exit price: **300% of Development Costs**.
- **§14.2.10 "Termination for JSC Decision"** — SFJ may terminate **"in its sole discretion"**, immediately, merely because it continues to disagree with a decision PB is contractually entitled to make; PB then pays Development Costs **plus 25% annual interest**.
- SFJ's other exits (§14.2.3 Material Adverse Event, §14.2.5 bankruptcy, §14.2.9 Adverse Patent Impact, §3.20 Program Transfer) are cause- or event-triggered, so not treated as convenience rights.

**Why it fails the fallback:** in a multi-year program PB has no exit for the first tranche of spend (or after first approval), while SFJ holds a near-convenience right on immediate notice — the latter is squarely in walk-away territory (provider convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice).

**Redline (validated ok:true), pitched at the fallback:**
1. §14.2.2 — remove the $60M threshold and the pre-approval window; fix notice at **thirty (30) days**.
2. Delete §14.2.10 and its payment consequence.

**Noted, not flagged:** the 300% exit payment exceeds the playbook's early-termination fee cap, but it is the priced return in this development-funding bargain, so pressing the preferred no-penalty position would be disproportionate.
